pr.title: Allow transmute casts in pre-runtime-MIR
pr.description:
r? @scottmcm

cc @BoxyUwU 

turns out in https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/138393 I erroneously used transmute casts in https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/fd3da4bebdff63b7529483ff7025986ef16bf463/compiler/rustc_mir_build/src/builder/matches/test.rs#L209

I don't think they have any issues using them before runtime, we just checked for them because we didn't have code exercising those code paths
pr.author: oli-obk

analysis.originalLogic: In the MIR `Validator` (`compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/validate.rs`), `CastKind::Transmute` was checked based on the body's MIR phase. If the body was in `MirPhase::Runtime(..)`, the validator normalized the operand and target types and required each to be `Sized`, failing with `Cannot transmute from non-`Sized` type {op_ty}` or `Cannot transmute to non-`Sized` type {target_type:?}`. For every non-runtime phase, it instead unconditionally failed with `Transmute is not supported in non-runtime phase {:?}`. The enum documentation in `compiler/rustc_middle/src/mir/syntax.rs` also stated `Transmute` was `Allowed only in [`MirPhase::Runtime`]; Earlier it's a [`TerminatorKind::Call`].`
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation was the phase-based rejection: treating a MIR `CastKind::Transmute` in any non-`MirPhase::Runtime` body as invalid and emitting `Transmute is not supported in non-runtime phase`, rather than applying the same sizedness well-formedness checks used for runtime MIR. After the fix, `Transmute` is accepted in pre-runtime MIR as well, and validation only checks that the normalized source and target types are `Sized`. This is a validator correctness fix, not an optimization: the old check rejected valid pre-runtime MIR even though the PR says `I don't think they have any issues using them before runtime`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies containing `CastKind::Transmute`, across MIR phases (pre-runtime/build MIR and `MirPhase::Runtime`), where the transmute operand and target type may be `Sized` or non-`Sized` after normalization. The changed test path is pre-runtime MIR generated for pattern-type pattern matching, checked with `-Zvalidate-mir`.
analysis.summary: The MIR `Validator` must permit `CastKind::Transmute` in pre-runtime MIR; the phase-based rejection was wrong. Validation should enforce only the well-formedness invariant that both the normalized operand and target types are `Sized`, because a MIR transmute is well-formed for any two `Sized` types but may be UB to execute.
analysis.trigger: Validating a MIR body whose phase is not `MirPhase::Runtime` and which contains a `CastKind::Transmute` cast.
preconditions: MIR validation is enabled (for example with `-Zvalidate-mir`).
The MIR body contains a `CastKind::Transmute` cast.
The body is in a non-runtime MIR phase, such as pre-runtime MIR emitted before runtime MIR lowering.
The transmute source and target types are both `Sized` (the valid case that the old phase gate incorrectly rejected).
pitfalls: Do not use the body's MIR phase as the validity criterion for `CastKind::Transmute`; pre-runtime transmute casts are allowed.
Do not omit the sizedness checks when moving them out of the runtime-only branch: both the normalized operand type and target type must still be `Sized`.
MIR `Transmute` is not identical to `mem::transmute`: the PR comment says a MIR `Transmute` is well-formed `for any two `Sized` types, just potentially UB to run.`
Pre-runtime MIR historically represented this operation as `TerminatorKind::Call`, but that does not make a pre-runtime `CastKind::Transmute` invalid.
A retained test name or a `check-pass` annotation alone is insufficient evidence; the actual regression change adds `-Zvalidate-mir` to exercise the pre-runtime path.
analysis.testStrategy: Use a UI test with `//@ check-pass` and `//@ compile-flags: -Zvalidate-mir` that produces pre-runtime MIR containing a transmute cast, as in `tests/ui/type/pattern_types/matching.rs` for pattern-type pattern matching. The PR adds `//@ compile-flags: -Zvalidate-mir` to `matching.rs`, exercising the previously rejected pre-runtime transmute path. Also keep focused negative validation coverage for non-`Sized` source or target types. Do not claim runtime execution or reproduction; this knowledge is derived from the patch and test changes only.
